checks.title: FC ESC socket vs ESC socket vs the lead
checks.evidence: ESC socket positions 1-8: Curr, NC, M4, M3, M2, M1, VBAT, GND (maker drawing). FC socket positions 1-8: Curr, RX7, M4, M3, M2, M1, VBAT, GND (ArduPilot port diagram, silk "C R 4 3 2 1 V G"). Maker wiring diagram draws a straight lead. On the robot both boards face rear with the sockets on the same (bottom) edge and in the same left-right order, so a straight lead (position n to n) is correct.
checks.open: Whether the stack box contains the 8-pin lead is not stated (listing: "1 x MicoAir 743 V2 Stack"); the SH kit in the cart makes one either way.

checks.title: ArduPilot Quad-X numbering, spin, ESC pad sets
checks.evidence: AP_MotorsMatrix QUAD X: motor 1 at +45 deg (front right) CCW, motor 2 at -135 (rear left) CCW, motor 3 at -45 (front left) CW, motor 4 at +135 (rear right) CW. ESC stood behind the right arm with tabs up puts pad sets 1 and 2 on the outboard (right) edge and 3 and 4 on the inboard edge, so outputs are remapped: SERVO1_FUNCTION 33 (pad 1 -> FR, motor 1), SERVO2_FUNCTION 36 (pad 2 -> RR, motor 4), SERVO3_FUNCTION 35 (pad 3 -> FL, motor 3), SERVO4_FUNCTION 34 (pad 4 -> RL, motor 2). Rotor spin seen from above (= from the inlet, inlets face up) must be CW at front-left and rear-right, CCW at front-right and rear-left. ARESWEI sells handed units: green motor = "CW" (B0H4KJLR6P), red motor = "CCW" (B0H4KSDT77) (seller claims), so planned placement is green at FL and RR, red at FR and RL, if the seller's CW is seen from the inlet. Direction: an EDF rotor is handed, so each unit must turn its own way to blow down; set it by swapping two leads at the bullets (ArduPilot wiki) or the AM32 "Reversed" box (MicoAir AM32 page).
checks.open: Which end ARESWEI's "CW" is seen from is not published. Rotation procedure, before the fans go into the nacelles (fan held in a clamp, inlet up, nothing near the inlet; Mission Planner Motor Test, 5 % for 2 s, one output at a time): (1) the motor test letter A to D must spin the fan planned for it (A = motor 1 FR, B = motor 4 RR, C = motor 2 RL, D = motor 3 FL in Quad-X test order); (2) airflow: a paper strip at the lip is pulled in and one under the motor end is blown away; if the air runs backwards, swap any two bullets of that fan (or tick AM32 Reversed) and repeat; (3) with air flowing the right way, look into the inlet from above: FL and RR must turn clockwise, FR and RL counterclockwise. If a green unit turns counterclockwise from above when it blows the right way, the seller's CW is seen from the motor end: swap green and red units side to side (FL<->FR, RR<->RL; re-plug the bullets, no soldering) and repeat (2) and (3). A unit in the wrong place still lifts but its torque reverses the yaw control, so the duck spins at take-off: step (3) is not optional.

checks.title: A7Z to FC MAVLink link
checks.evidence: Free A7Z pins: 14 (GND), 16 (PJ24, UART4-TX), 18 (PJ25, UART4-RX); not in the as-built 19-wire map (used: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 9 11 12 17 25 29 31 34 35 38 39 40). UART2 (pins 7/11) carries the servo bus and is not touched; UART3 is on the IMU pins 3/5; UART0 (8/10) is the debug console. Radxa's stock overlay sun60iw2p1-uart4 ("Enable UART4", compatible radxa,cubie-a7z, "pin 16 and pin 18") gives /dev/ttyAS4. Levels: PJ bank VCC-PJ = VCC33-LCD 3.3 V (schematic V1.11); STM32H743 UART at 3.3 V; no level shifter needed. FC: SERIAL1 (UART1), default MAVLink2.
checks.open: A spare UART has never been enabled on this A7Z: CURRENT-STATE lists only the TWI7, TWI0, I2S0 overlays and UART2; no session enabled uart4 (transcript search "ttyAS4": documentation mentions only). The A7Z was offline on 2026-11-10 (ssh timeout), so /dev/ttyAS* was not read. Physical access to pins 14/16/18 in the saddle (edge row) not seen on the robot. 921600 baud on the A7Z UART is untested (115200 fallback).

checks.title: Two packs in parallel into the ESC tabs; currents vs ratings
checks.evidence: Mass used: all-up 1883 to 1897 g with the ARESWEI fans; hover thrust 471-474 g per fan (48 % of the seller's 980 g). Hover current per fan 15.1-28.1 A (three methods: {'vendor': [15.1, 15.3], 'bench': [27.8, 28.1], 'momentum': [22.5, 22.8]}; {'vendor': 'P = 672 W x (T / 980 g)^1.5 / 14.8 V (seller point 980 g at 16.8 V and 40 A, momentum-theory scaling)', 'bench': 'same with max thrust 2/3 of the seller figure (independent tests of similar 50 mm fans, PET log)', 'momentum': 'ideal annulus power / 0.5 (rotor 49.0 mm, hub 23 mm, seller drawing)'}), total 60-112 A. Peak per fan 40 A (seller claim, "peak working current of 40A" at 16.8 V), 160 A total uncapped. Right pack share 53% (shorter pigtail). Per pack: hover 32.1-59.6 A, peak 84.8 A uncapped, 58.3 A with MOT_BAT_CURR_MAX 110. Ratings: ESC 55 A per channel vs fan 40 A peak: pass (15 A margin). Pack 130C x 1.3 Ah = 169 A claimed vs at most 84.8 A per pack: pass. XT60 (Amass) rated 30 A, max 60 A: low hover case inside the rating, high hover case at the maximum; peaks stay at or under 60 A only with the MOT_BAT_CURR_MAX cap. 12 AWG chassis 41 A: hover at most at that figure, flights 1-1.5 min. 16 AWG chassis 22 A vs per-fan hover rms (0.82 x DC in six-step) and 40 A bursts: see motor_leads. Harness: one male XT60 pigtail per pack, both soldered to the same ESC tab pair; no Y-splice.
checks.open: The hover current spans about 2x between methods (15.1 vs 28.1 A per fan) and decides the outcome. Low case (about 60 A total): the right XT60 carries about 32.1 A, at about its 30 A rating, and the 110 A cap leaves about 1.8x control headroom. High case (about 112 A total): the right XT60 carries about 59.6 A continuous, at its 60 A maximum, and hover alone reaches the 110 A cap, so it cannot climb; the cap would have to rise and the XT60s would run above their maximum. The fix then is soldering the pack leads straight to the pigtails or fitting XT90s (nothing different to order now: the packs and wire stay). Decided by the first tethered hover: read BATT current (after BATT_AMP_PERVLT 78.43) and feel the XT60 bodies after 60 s. A flight-envelope limit, not a wiring blocker.

checks.title: Ground and supply separation between duck and flight pack
checks.evidence: Joined: exactly one conductor, FC UART1 position 1 (GND) to A7Z pin 14 (GND), plus the two UART signal lines. Open: FC UART1 position 2 (5V); A7Z 5 V pins 2/4 untouched; no other conductor between the systems (printed frame, no metal path). No loop in flight: the only return path between the two negatives is that one 28 AWG wire, and no load current has a reason to flow in it. Back-feed: no 5 V or VBAT crosses. The one weak case: with the A7Z off and the FC powered, FC TX1 idles at 3.3 V into PJ25 of an unpowered SoC (through its protection diode, a few mA). Rule: duck on before the flight packs, flight packs off first (or unplug the 3-pin lead).
checks.open: If the FC USB and an A7Z USB cable go to the same Mac at the same time, the Mac ground joins them a second time: harmless at bench currents, do not hover like that.

checks.title: Motor lead length and extensions
checks.evidence: Fan leads about 140 mm with 3.5 mm male bullets (seller: "Pre-wired 3.5mm bullet connectors"; the drawing label reads "55.1 inch", a misplaced decimal: drawn to scale the leads are 5.5 in). Routed distances from cad/checks/lead_lengths.json, extension = route + 20 mm - lead: FR 149 mm -> lead reaches; 40 mm stub, 11 mm spare lead tied, RR 70 mm -> lead reaches; 40 mm stub, 90 mm spare lead tied, FL 305 mm -> 190 mm extension, RL 217 mm -> 100 mm extension. Every pad set still gets three 16 AWG wires with a 3.5 mm female bullet: the bullet needs a wire to sit on and the fan must unplug at its nacelle. 16 AWG over 190 mm at 40 A: 13.2 mOhm/m, two phases conduct, drop about 0.20 V; rms per phase about 33 A, above the 22 A chassis figure, so full throttle is a burst of seconds; hover rms 12-23 A is at that figure. Fan lead gauge is not published. Long motor leads with short battery leads is the ESC-friendly split; the left side has both, unavoidable with one ESC on the right.
checks.open: Lead length and bullet size are seller figures: measure on arrival (2026-11-12). If a lead is shorter than 140 mm, the FL and RL extensions grow by the difference (cut from the same 16 AWG stock).

checks.title: Arm and stop without an RC receiver
checks.evidence: No extra hardware. Parameters (Copter 4.6.3 sources): FS_THR_ENABLE 0 (no RC throttle failsafe); ARMING_CHECK with bit 6 "RC Channels" cleared (1047998 = all individual checks except RC); arm, mode changes and take-off from the A7Z over MAVLink (MAV_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM, GUIDED, MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF); stop = disarm, force with param2 21196; FS_GCS_ENABLE 5 (Land), FS_GCS_TIMEOUT 2 (minimum); the A7Z is the GCS (heartbeats at sysid 255 = SYSID_MYGCS default) and must land on its own if the web page stops (the FC only sees the A7Z). GCS failsafe only arms after a GCS has been seen, which arming from the A7Z guarantees. The board has no safety switch.
checks.open: Bench test before the first hover: kill the web page -> A7Z lands; kill the A7Z link -> FC lands after 2 s.

checks.open: Set BATT_AMP_PERVLT 78.43 at setup; check against a clamp meter or the charger's mAh refill.

checks.title: AM32 motor KV and pole count
checks.evidence: KV 4650 (seller claim) replaces the AM32 default 2220 (MicoAir AM32 page). The pole count is not published. What a wrong value affects, from the AM32 source (main.c at 077b6a4): motor_poles never enters commutation, which follows the back-EMF zero crossings; it only scales the low-RPM duty-limit window (low_rpm_level = KV / 100 / (32 / poles), high_rpm_level = KV / 12 / (32 / poles)), the sine-start step (only with sine start on) and the RPM speed-control mode (not used with DShot throttle). A wrong count therefore shifts the start-up throttle limit, not whether the motor runs. In ArduPilot SERVO_BLH_POLES only converts eRPM to true RPM ("This allows calculation of true RPM from ESC's eRPM"): logs and the ESC-RPM harmonic notch filter would sit at the wrong frequency. Finding it on the bench: (a) look through the motor can vents and count the magnets (poles = magnets; small 50 mm EDF outrunners are commonly 12N14P or 9N6P, inference); (b) or with bidirectional DShot on, run one fan at a steady low throttle, read the ESC eRPM in Mission Planner (ESC telemetry with SERVO_BLH_POLES 2 gives eRPM directly), and record the fan sound with a phone spectrum app: the strongest line is the blade-passing frequency f = RPM / 60 x 11 blades, so poles = 2 x eRPM / (60 x f / 11).
checks.open: Set AM32 Motor poles and SERVO_BLH_POLES to the counted value; until then leave 14 (the motor still commutates; only RPM readings and the low-RPM limit are off).
